# Tobit Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1:1** A-book of-words of-Tobit son-of Tobiel son-of Ananiel son-of Aduel son-of Gabael son-of Raphael son-of Raguel, from-the seed of Asiel, from-the tribe of Naphtali,

**1:2** who was-taken-captive in-the days of Enemessar the-king of-the Assyrians, out-of Thisbe, which is to-the right of Kedesh of-Naphtali in-the upper[-land] Galilee, above Asher, toward [the] west, in-front-of Phogor.

**1:3** I, Tobit, walked in-ways of truth and in-righteous-deeds all-the days of-my life. And many acts-of-mercy I-did to my brothers and my people, the-ones having-gone-up with me in-the land of-the Assyrians, into Nineveh.

**1:4** And when I-was in-my land, in-the land of Israel, [being] young, the whole tribe of Naphtali my-father departed from-the house of Jerusalem, which was-chosen from out-of all-the tribes of Israel for all-the tribes to-sacrifice therein, and in-which the temple of-the dwelling of-the Most-High was-consecrated and was-built for all-the generations of-the age.

**1:5** And all-the tribes that-joined-in-revolt together-with them and the-house of Jeroboam my-father's-father, they were-sacrificing to-the heifer Baal.

**1:6** But I alone was-going-up often to Jerusalem in-the feasts, as it-has-been-commanded to all Israel with-an everlasting ordinance, having-the firstfruits and the-tithes of-the produce and the-firstborn, and the-first-shearings of-the sheep,

**1:7** and I-was-giving them to-the priests, the sons of Aaron, at-the altar; and the-tithe of-the grain and the-wine and the-olive-oil and pomegranates and the-figs and the-remainder of-the fruits I-was-giving to-the sons of Levi, the ones ministering in Jerusalem; and the-second tithe in-silver I-was-redeeming six years [in a row] and was-going-up and was-spending [it] each year in Jerusalem;

**1:8** and the-third [tithe] I-was-giving to-the orphans and the-widows and to-the proselytes who were-attaching-themselves to-the children of Israel. I-was-bringing [them] and was-giving every third year, and we-were-eating [it] according-to the-ordinance that-had-been-commanded concerning it in-the law of Moses and according-to the-commands which Deborah the-mother of Ananiel our-father had-commanded us — for my-father had-died and left me an-orphan.

**1:9** And when I-was-made-full-grown, I-took a woman from-the seed of our-father's-house, Anna [by] name, and she-bore to-me Tobias.

**1:10** And after I-was-taken-captive into Assyria and I-came as-a-captive to Nineveh, all my brothers and those of-my race were-eating from-the breads of-the nations,

**1:11** but I myself kept-guard [over] my-soul and did-not eat,

**1:12** because I-remembered God with my-whole soul.

**1:13** And the-Most-High gave to-me grace and appearance in-the sight of Enemessar, and I-became his purchasing-agent.

**1:14** And I-was-going to Media and I-was-buying for him until he-died. And I-deposited in trust in-the hands of Gabael the-brother of Gabrias, in Media, [money-bags of] silver, ten talents.

**1:15** And when Enemessar died, Sennacherib his-son reigned in-his place. And the roads of Media became unsafe and I-could-no-longer journey into Media.

**1:16** And in-the days of Enemessar I-was-doing many acts-of-mercy to my brothers:

**1:17** my bread I-was-giving to-the hungry and clothing to-the naked; and if I-saw any of-my-race dead and thrown-out on-the wall of Nineveh, I-was-burying him.

**1:18** And whomever Sennacherib the-king was-killing when-he-returned [in-flight] from Judea, in-the days of the-judgment that-the-King of Heaven executed upon him on-account-of the-blasphemies which he-had-blasphemed — I-was-burying them in-secret; for in-his anger he-was-killing many from the sons of Israel — and I-was-stealing their corpses and was-burying [them], and Sennacherib was-seeking them and was-not-finding [them].

**1:19** But a certain one of-the Ninevites went and informed [of] me to-the king that I myself was-burying them and I-had-fled. And when I-learned that I-had-been-made-known to-the king and that I-was-sought to-be-put-to-death, I-was-afraid and I-fled.

**1:20** And all-the-things belonging-to-me were-seized, and nothing was-left-behind to-me, except Anna my-wife and Tobias my-son.

**1:21** And forty days did-not pass before two of-his sons killed him and they-fled to-the mountains of Ararat. And Sarchedonus his-son reigned in-his place; and he-appointed Achiacharus the-son of Anael my-brother's-son over all-the accounts of his-kingdom and over all-the administration.

**1:22** And Achiacharus interceded for me and I-returned to Nineveh. Now Achiacharus was chief-cup-bearer and keeper-of-the-ring and steward and accountant; and Sarchedonus appointed him as second [man]; and he-was my-brother's-son, [and from] of-my family.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

- 1:1: The genealogy in Sinaiticus (GII) is notably longer than in Vaticanus (GI), which reads only "son of Tobiel, son of Ananiel, son of Aduel, son of Gabael." The extended chain in GII may reflect a Semitic source that preserves tribal memory.
- 1:2: "to the right" (ek dexiōn) is a geographic directional; some translate "south" but EMET preserves the literal spatial sense.
- 1:4: "dwelling of the Most-High" (tou hypsistou) is used throughout Tobit in place of the divine name; EMET preserves "Most-High" consistently.
- 1:7: The third-tithe reckoning (1:7-8) corresponds to Deuteronomic legislation (Deut 14:28-29, 26:12); the narrative detail of Deborah as instructing grandmother is unique to GII.
- 1:8: "proselytes" translates prosēlytois — those attached to Israel; some render "converts."
- 1:13: "purchasing-agent" (agora-stēs) — one who purchases goods; some render "purveyor" or "buyer." EMET hyphenates to show compound function.
- 1:18: The phrase "King of Heaven" (ho basileus tou ouranou) is a distinctive Tobit usage; appears also in Daniel.
- 1:21: Sinaiticus has forty days (tessarakonta); the shorter recension differs on the chronology here.

*— EMET*
